children: plans to invest $3B in India’s quick-commerce business by 2030, Reuters reported on Thursday.
The company plans to invest $1B by the end of 2027 and another $2B by 2030, according to two people with direct knowledge of the plans who spoke to Reuters.
The U.S. retailer is seeking to expand in a market where rivals have built a large lead in fast deliveries.
AMZN did not immediately respond to Seeking Alpha's request for a comment.
Amazon's quick-commerce business, Amazon Now, had surpassed $1B in annualized gross sales over the past three months, according to Reuters.

The investment will focus in part on expanding Amazon Now’s network of small neighborhood warehouses, allowing the company to fulfill orders closer to customers and speed up deliveries, the sources said.
Quick commerce has grown rapidly in India since 2022, with companies delivering groceries, household goods, and electronics within minutes. Walmart-owned
Flipkart and Amazon have entered the market later than companies that helped popularize the model.
India’s quick-commerce market is expected to more than double to $41B by 2030 from $19B, according to Datum Intelligence.
The rapid growth has also drawn scrutiny over rider safety and operating practices. In January, India’s government told companies to stop promoting quick-commerce services as “10-minute” deliveries.

title: Amazon plans a $3B India quick-commerce investment by 2030: report
